title: Siegard reconciliation record
description: One record of a reconciliation: source that changed without a rebind — whatever wrote it — the specification nodes the trace says that source encodes, and the judgment's answer per node. It lives at `siegard-reconcile/<slug>.md` beside `siegard.json` and `siegard-trace.json`, in the target source root's git toplevel, because what it justifies is a bind and a bind outlives every plan and delivery root. It exists for one reason: every other bind this framework writes is backed by an implementation record that says which node the source encodes and why, and a bind performed on a hand edit would otherwise rest on a judgment held nowhere — a decision nobody can reopen, which is exactly what the determinism rules forbid. `bin/trace.py --reconciliation` validates it; `bin/trace.py --bind-record` then writes exactly the bindings it states. The two halves are joined mechanically rather than by prose: a pair the judgment did not clear is under no `encoded_at`, and `--bind-record` reads only the pairs that are — so a record of a reconciliation that stopped binds nothing without any second rule saying it must not. That join is per pair, and so is the act: a record whose judgment cleared some pairs and not others writes the ones it cleared and none of the rest, which is why every entry below states its own answer and carries its own evidence. Nothing is claimed about the set. A node with a finding against it stays exactly as it stood, while every binding written rests on the judgment that cleared that node and on nothing else here; the bind's receipt names what it did not write, so a partial reconciliation never reads like a complete one. What `--check` says about that node afterwards depends on whether the pair was bound before, and often it says nothing: drift is computed from the bindings, so a finding against a pair no binding holds — a node the judge opened as a candidate, bound to a sibling file and not to this one — has no digest to disagree with, and a later bind that stamps the very content the finding was read in removes the only digest that did. This is why the record is the account and not a note beside one: `trace.py --owed` reads these files back, and without them the finding exists nowhere a reader can reach. Refusing the whole record over one finding would have made a judgment that resolved most of a set worth exactly what one that resolved none is worth, and paid to read every cleared file again. Nothing here is pinned. The bind pins both sides at the moment it is written, and a second copy of those digests here would be a second home that goes stale the day either side moves.

targetPath.description: Relative to the target source root, exactly as `siegard-trace.json` and every delivery record spell a path. One anchor or none of them can be compared: the file set the human named, the paths a node's binding holds, and the paths this record accounts for are matched against each other by spelling. Never absolute, and never spelled from the repository around the target.

specNodeRef.description: A specification node, by identity — «Identity is the node's path from the specification root, without `.md`» (SPEC-003 R1).

commit.description: A git commit, by its full object name: the history a pinned text is recovered from. Abbreviated, it would be a name the repository may later make ambiguous.

contract_version.description: Which contract this record was written against. siegard-reconcile/2 carried one boolean per node over a question that is two: whether the source still states what the node holds, and whether it states a fact no node holds at all. The second answer landed on whichever node the file happened to be bound to, blocked a binding its own reading had cleared, and could never be closed by any rebind — so /3 made `unstated` its own list, and `conforms` answers the pair alone. /4 lets a cleared node carry a certification: a judgment found a test that would fail if the node's fact stopped holding, and named the step that runs it, so `--bind-record` writes the binding as one a test decides. /6 lets a record adopt source no delivery wrote: `adopted` says the candidates an analysis wrote from that source were judged on every file, a cleared node carries under `encoded_at` the files that hold its fact and no others, and `outside` names the tracked files the human kept out of the judgment. /7 keeps an adoption's candidate that no file of the set holds out of `nodes`: it is listed under `unheld`, claiming no file, and a candidate a finding stands against names under `observed_at` the files the finding was read in, beside every file the trace already binds it to, and no others — a /6 record named every judged file for both, which reads as one open finding per file. /8 lists apart, under `restates`, the places text in the source restates a node's fact the code holds: the pair conforms and binds, where a /7 record's judge filed the same observation as `contradicts` and the node stayed unbound. /9 pins a refused certification at what it was read at, under `read_at`: the node's digest and each offered proof file's, as the staging took them — so a later staging can tell an unchanged pair from one that moved, and name the record it rests on; a /8 record carries none, which is not a count of zero. /10 answers each pair by its own file's judgment: a node whose fact left part of its ground — still held in some bound files, read `nowhere` in another, with nothing found against it — stays not cleared, and carries under `encoded_at` the files that still hold it, which `--bind-record` binds; the pair read `nowhere` is a release a person decides. A /9 record left those holders unbound and reported as drift by every later check. /11 lets a record carry, under `rewritten`, the pairs a rewrite the human declared reproduces exactly from the text each binding pinned, answered by a run of the steps the declaration names and by no judge; a /10 record carries none, which is not a count of zero. A /2 to /10 record is the reading it was, read by tolerant readers, never rewritten to match.

title.description: What was reconciled, in a line.

summary.description: What changed in the source and why the human states it is correct. This is the premise the whole record rests on and it is a human's assertion, never the judgment's: the pass below decides whether the specification still holds, not whether the code is right.

target.description: Which of the project's target source roots this reconciliation reaches, by the key `siegard.json`'s `targets` names it. A record is read long after the invocation that wrote it, and a path anchor whose root nobody named anchors nothing.

files.description: The file set the human named, and nothing else. Never discovered: a reconciliation that chose its own scope reconciles a different set each run, and the bindings it writes would claim ground nobody declared. Every path a node below accounts for must appear here, and every path here must be accounted for by a node or by `unbound`.

change.description: What the file now does differently, not what was typed into it. A diff says what changed; this says what changed about the behavior, which is the only form the judgment below can be held to.

nodes.description: Every specification node the trace binds to a named file, with the judgment's answer for it. Empty only where the trace binds none of them — which is a real outcome, not an omission, and `unbound` is where it is recorded. The set is read from the trace's own bindings, never chosen: which nodes a file answers to is what the trace holds, and picking a subset of them would reconcile a file against the part of the specification that happened to agree with it. `trace.py --check` names the drifted ones and is where a reconciliation starts, but it is not the whole set — a drift report says nothing about a file whose binding is intact, and those nodes are read from `siegard-trace.json` itself. An orphaned binding is the exception: its node is gone from the specification, no bind repairs it, and `--prune` is its route. `--bind-record` refuses a record that leaves a bound node unanswered.

allOf.$comment: The two field names are what makes the rule structural instead of pious. `bin/trace.py --bind-record` binds every path under `encoded_at` and reads nothing else, so a pair the judgment did not clear cannot be bound from this record however the caller invokes it. On a node not cleared, `encoded_at` is the pairs of `observed_at` whose own judgment holds the fact, written only where nothing was found against the node, and `--reconciliation` refuses one naming a path its `observed_at` does not.
A cleared node cannot be collateral: the mark exists to tell a blocked-only-by-a-sibling-finding node from a contested one, and both readings presuppose the node stands unbound.

Either answer to the certification question rides a cleared node. A node the judgment did not clear is bound by nothing here, so what decides it is not this record's to say: the standing binding is left exactly as it stood.
A certification names its test and its step, or it is not one; every other answer names neither. A node that carries a test without claiming certification is a shape nobody meant.
A remainder exists only where a certification was asked and refused: what a test could still close is a fact about a node decided by reading, and neither half stands without the other.

conforms.description: Whether the source, as it now stands, still states only what this node holds. It is the conformance judgment's answer, delegated and read — never the caller's own reading of the file, and never inferred from the edit having been small.

collateral.description: Present only on a node the judgment did not clear, and only where nothing was found against the node's own substance: its file carried a finding that named no node, and the conservative default — an unattributed finding lands on every node of the file its judge read — is the whole of why this node stands unbound. A reader routing the open findings reads this as 'route the unattributed finding, then re-judge; nothing here contests the node itself'. Never present on a node any finding names directly.

how.description: Why the answer above is the answer, with what was read quoted rather than restated. Where it conforms, this says which part of the file carries the node's fact now. Where it does not, this says what the source states that the node does not hold, or states differently — quoted, because a judgment whose evidence cannot be quoted is a judgment nobody made. Findings as a contract live in `delivery-node.json`, owned by the review that produces them; this field states the same observation in prose rather than opening a second home for the shape.

encoded_at.description: The file(s) of the set above that encode this node: on a node the judgment cleared, every file that holds it; on a node whose fact left part of its ground with nothing found against it, the files that still hold it, each of them also under `observed_at`. This is the list `--bind-record` binds, so it is the whole of what this record claims: a path here is a path the trace will assert answers to this node. Every entry must be in `files`.

observed_at.description: The file(s) of the set above the judgment read for this node, on a node it did not clear and nowhere else — the files that still hold it among them, where `encoded_at` names those: on an adoption, the files a finding was read in and every file the trace already binds the node to, whether or not that file still holds it — a bound pair the record leaves unnamed is one no bind can account for. It records what was looked at without claiming anything about it, which is why the accounting below can still reach every named file while nothing is bound. Every entry must be in `files`.

decided_by.description: What this reconciliation found decides the node, present only where it asked. `test`: a judgment certified that the tests under `proof` would fail if the node's fact stopped holding — the whole test of a test, applied by the auditor whose rule it is and never by the caller — and `--bind-record` writes the binding as one a test decides. `reading`: it asked and the auditor refused, so the bind releases any certification standing on the node from an earlier reconciliation; saying it structurally is what keeps the trace from going on deciding by a test a judgment has just found cannot fail, while this record's notes say the node is decided by reading. Absent: this reconciliation did not ask, and a standing certification is none of its business — the bind carries it forward while its proof's text stands. Written from the auditor's return alone, never from a node's type: `policy` and `invariant` say what kind of rule a node is, not whether a test settles it.

step.description: The registry step that runs the proof, by the name `commands[].step` gives it, as the human named it to the staging. The staging refuses a step the registry does not declare.

proof.description: The test file(s) the auditor cited as bearing on the fact — never the whole set the human offered, which the auditor may cite in part. A file offered and not cited bears on nothing the certification rests on, and pinning it would let an edit to it lapse a certification no reading of it supported; the fold writes the cited set and `--bind-record` pins exactly that. Spelled from the target source root like every path here; not required to be in `files`, because the tests are read to certify and never reconciled by this record.

remainder.description: On a node a certification left decided by reading: whether the part of the fact the offered tests leave unexercised is one a test could assert, or a fact no finite test closes. Carried from the auditor's return and never written from a node's type. `testable` is the one this record hands forward — `--owed` lists such nodes as the work a test closes, because a node a certified test decides pays no judge, and a file pays none once every binding on it is decided by a step or a test. `untestable` is said once, here, and handed to nothing: a fact no test closes is decided by reading for as long as it is stated as it is, and a list that repeated it would be a floor rather than a finding. Never reaches the trace: what decides the binding is `reading`, and the trace already says so.

remainder_why.description: The auditor's sentence beside the remainder: the assertion a test would make to close a testable one, or what no finite test asserts of an untestable one. Carried verbatim.

read_at.description: On a node a certification left decided by reading, and nowhere else: what the auditor read, pinned — the node's text digest and each offered proof file's digest, as the staging took them. A refusal written without it reads like a reading that could be any reading; with it, a later staging can say that nothing moved since, name this record, and leave the pair to a person's own re-read. The judgment is not reused: what is compared is bytes, never the auditor's answer.

unstated.description: Facts the named source states that no node of the specification holds — found while reading these files against these nodes, and owed to the analysis rather than to any binding here. Absent where the judgments found none. It is deliberately not keyed by node: a fact no node holds has no node to be about, and attaching it to whichever node shared its file is what made a correct binding wait on a finding no rebind could close. Nothing here blocks a bind, and `--owed` reports it apart from what does.

file.description: The named file that states it, as the premise spells it.

where.description: Where in that file the fact is stated.

evidence.description: Quoted from the source — the code that states it, never a comment's claim about it.

cost.description: What the specification's silence costs here, in terms a reader can weigh.

restates.description: Every place a judge read a comment or a docstring — prose no running system emits — restating a fact a node holds while code holds it too. Listed apart from the nodes because the pair conforms: none blocks a binding, and what each owes is the text's removal by the route that answers prose, with the file reconciled after. `trace.py --owed` lists them apart from what a bind is owed.

unbound.description: Named files the trace holds no binding for. They are reported and never guessed at: deciding which node an untraced file answers to is a delivery's judgment or an analysis's, and inventing one here would write the framework's most durable claim out of the least evidence. On an adoption a file listed here is one no candidate was cleared in and no finding named; which files an adoption judged and bound nothing to is what `trace.py --untraced` counts as holds-nothing. Every entry must be in `files`, and none may also appear under a node.

adopted.description: This record adopts source no delivery wrote — «A binding of adopted source rests on a reconciliation record whose judgment cleared the pair» (SPEC-005 R3). Every candidate node was read on every file of the set, and a cleared node's `encoded_at` names the files whose judgment holds its fact and no others. Absent on every other reconciliation, where a cleared node holds its fact in every file the trace binds it to.

unheld.description: An adoption's candidates that no file of the set holds and nothing was found against: every judge that read one answered `nowhere`. Listed apart from `nodes` because the answer is about the node and not about any pair — it claims no file and owes no reading; it is the analysis's to revisit, or the adoption of the files that do hold it. Only an adopted record carries it.

outside.description: Tracked files the human kept out of an adoption's judgment: no judge read them and nothing here says what they hold. Named so that a file kept out is never read afterwards as one that was judged and found empty. Only an adopted record carries it, and none of its entries is in `files`.

rewritten.description: The pairs a rewrite the human declared carries to the file as it stands, without a judgment — «A pair whose file changed by a rewrite the reconciliation declares is carried to the file as it stands without a judgment, where the declared rewrite applied to the text the binding pinned reproduces the current text exactly and every step the declaration names passed over that tree» (SPEC-005 R11). The rewrite and its claim to change no behavior are the human's, like `summary`; what this framework adds is the evidence: the text each binding pinned, recovered from git at `pinned_at` and run through the rewrite, equals the file's current bytes, and the run named here passed every step the declaration names. A pair listed here was read by no judge, so it is no reading in the corpus: `--owed` counts it neither as a clearance nor as a finding. Whether it binds is still said by its node's entry under `nodes`, where it sits under `encoded_at` or `observed_at` like any pair, and `--bind-record` recomputes every reproduction before it writes anything.

pattern.description: The declared rewrite's pattern, as Python's `re` reads it, verbatim from the declaration. The framework knows no language: what the pattern rewrites, and why that changes no behavior, is the declaration's.

replacement.description: The declared rewrite's replacement, as `re.sub` reads it, verbatim from the declaration.

steps.description: The registry steps the declaration names, by `commands[].step`; every one must have passed over the tree for any pair here to bind. The reproduction says the text is the old text rewritten; the run says the rewritten tree still builds and passes.

run.description: The run that answered the steps, as `bin/run.py` named it under this reconciliation's returns directory.

pairs.description: Every pair the rewrite reproduced, with the commit whose tree holds the text the binding pinned. A pair absent here was judged or omitted, never carried.

proofs.description: The certified tests of a carried node whose text moved, each reproduced by the same rewrite from the text the certification pinned. A node listed here keeps its certification live: `--bind-record` restamps each test's digest. A node one of whose moved tests the rewrite does not reproduce is listed nowhere here, and its certification stays as it stood — decided by reading until a judgment certifies the test as it now stands.

pairs_omitted.description: Bound node-file pairs this reconciliation did not re-judge, each with the reason. A pair may be omitted only where the judgment it would buy already exists: the binding computes at the file's content as it stands now — the pair was judged over these exact bytes and stamped — and no reconciliation record holds an open finding against it. Both halves are recomputed by `--bind-record` at the moment of binding, never taken from this list: a pair listed here that turns out stale or owed refuses the whole record. Re-judging a pair that satisfies both is buying a second reading of text that did not move, and what a second reading of unchanged input adds is not confidence. A file whose every pair is omitted is accounted for by this list the way a judged file is accounted for by its nodes. A review omits more narrowly — only a pair whose trace entry carries `judged`, never a pair of a node it names under `--node` — and its reason says the pair was cleared by a judgment at these bytes; for such a pair `--bind-record` also requires `judged` to stand at the moment of binding.

reason.description: Why the pair was omittable, as a standing fact — the binding current, no finding owed.

notes.description: Anything a later reader needs that the fields above have no home for — a node the trace reported as bound to a specification node that no longer exists, a merge this edit came out of, a second file the fact may have moved to. Prose, and never a decision.

examples.title: Certified: a placed order answers its number
examples.summary: place() is asserted correct as it stands; this reconciliation reads it against its node and certifies the test that proves the node, so that later drift on the file is decided by the suite.

files.change: unchanged; read to certify the test that proves domain/sales/order

nodes.how: the node's identity is `order_number`, and `return persisted.order_number` is what the entry point answers with

examples.notes: Certified by the coverage auditor: `it('answers the persisted order_number')` fails when place() answers anything else, so the pair is decided by the `test` step from here on.

examples.title: Certification of invoice immutability did not hold
examples.summary: raise() is asserted correct as it stands; the test offered for rules/sales/invoice-immutable exercises the refusal and not the immutability, so the node stays decided by reading, with the test that would close it named.

files.change: unchanged; read to certify the test offered for rules/sales/invoice-immutable

nodes.how: `if (invoice.raised) throw new ImmutableInvoice()` guards every setter the file exports, which is the rule's whole statement
nodes.remainder_why: one input — an alteration to a raised invoice's amount — against one expected result, a refusal that leaves the invoice as it stood

examples.notes: Certification of rules/sales/invoice-immutable did not hold: the auditor answered `partial` — the refusal half is exercised; nothing in the set alters a raised invoice's amount. The node is decided by reading. The remainder is testable.

examples.title: Hand correction to order placement
examples.summary: place() was returning the stored row rather than the order_number; corrected by hand during an incident and confirmed correct against the running system.

files.change: answers with the persisted order_number instead of the row it was written from

nodes.how: the node's identity is `order_number`, and `return persisted.order_number` is now what the entry point answers with; nothing in the file states a fact the node does not hold

examples.title: Hand correction to invoicing
examples.summary: The nightly run raised two invoices for one order; the guard was added by hand and the behavior is correct.

files.change: refuses a second invoice for an order that already has one

nodes.how: the source now states `if (order.invoices.length >= 1) return existing`, and no node holds that an order carries at most one invoice — the rule the file cites governs modification of a raised invoice, not how many may be raised

examples.notes: The behavior is right and the specification is behind it; the fact belongs in a node before anything is bound.
